title: Education Benefits Reductions and Withdrawals - Effective Dates and Resulting Debts
content:
**Policy statement — changes in enrollment, Education Benefits (GI Bill and Dependents' Education).**

**(a) Effective date.** When a student reduces credits or withdraws, the change is effective on the term start date unless VA accepts mitigating circumstances, in which case it is effective on the last date of attendance.

**(b) Mitigating circumstances.** The first 6 credit hours a student ever drops are accepted as mitigating without evidence. Other reasons — serious illness, a family emergency, military orders — require evidence.

**(c) Overpayment to the student.** Payments already issued for days after the effective date beyond what the amended enrollment supports become an overpayment. The amount is the housing and flat monthly payments issued for the amended certification covering days from the effective date — the term start date where no mitigating circumstances apply — through the term end date, less what the amended enrollment supports for those days. It is established as the tier's debt type for housing, books and flat monthly payments.

**(d) Tuition and fees overpayment.** A tuition and fees overpayment is established against the school when the change took effect before the term started and the tier makes such a debt the school's; it is established under the tier's tuition and fees debt type against the student otherwise.

| Change took effect before the term started | Tier makes a pre-start tuition debt the school's | Debt established against |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | The school |
| Yes | No | The student, under the tier's tuition and fees debt type |
| No | Yes or No | The student, under the tier's tuition and fees debt type |

**(e) Entitlement — retired clause.** The clause "Entitlement charged for days no longer certified is restored" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for giving back entitlement after an amended enrollment.

**(f) School refunds.** Tuition the school refunds is recorded as a return.

**Illustration (hypothetical).** A student drops a course mid-term and VA accepts mitigating circumstances on evidence of a family emergency: the change is effective on the last date of attendance. Had no mitigating circumstances been accepted, it would be effective on the term start date, and housing or monthly payments issued for the days from the term start beyond what the remaining enrollment supports would become the overpayment under (c).

superseded_clauses: Entitlement charged for days no longer certified is restored
